about: written by case.py; board_summary.py puts it on the page

printed.name: Body
printed.why: the rounded bottom edge (radius 4) rises gently from the bed; nothing hangs in the air

printed.name: Deck
printed.why: the posts and the rim grow straight up from a flat plate

print_settings: PLA, 0.2 mm layers, 0.4 mm nozzle, 4 walls (the 2.4 mm walls print solid), 20 % infill, no supports: the 3D printing rules of thumb in docs/fusion_reference.md
assembly: Solder the parts onto the board: the ESP32 straight on (its pin strips' plastic on the board), the screen, the buzzer (+ to the square pad), the six buttons. Clip the leads under the board to 2 mm or less.
Screw the board onto the deck's four posts: 4 x M3 x 8 from above, through the board's holes. Turn each one until it is snug, no further: it cuts its thread in the plastic.
Lay the power bank in the body, its ports toward the left grip, and plug the short cable's USB-A into it.
Feed the cable's other end up through the slot in the deck's left grip, lay the deck on the body and screw it down: 4 x M3 x 10 into the columns in the grips.
Plug the cable into the ESP32's micro-USB, at the gap in the rim. Charge the bank through the port bay in the left end.
assumed: this is an example for learning, not made for production: the bank is the owner's 100 x 70 x 15 mm, its USB port taken at the middle of its left end; the parts' heights are their common sizes
